sections.title: Async Retry Pattern — Coding Challenges — Advanced Async Patterns
sections.body:
```
╔═════════════════════��════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  CODING CHALLENGES — Advanced Async Patterns                 ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Challenge 1: [Producer-Consumer]
  Build a "multi-stage ETL pipeline" with:
  - Stage 1: 3 producers fetching data from different APIs
  - Stage 2: 5 transformer workers (data cleaning/enrichment)
  - Stage 3: 2 loader workers (save to DB)
  - Each stage connected by bounded asyncio.Queue
  - Monitor throughput and backpressure at each stage

Challenge 2: [Rate Limiter]
  Implement a "distributed rate limiter" that:
  - Limits requests across multiple async workers
  - Supports per-user rate limits (user_id → N req/sec)
  - Uses Redis (simulate with dict) for shared state
  - Handles burst traffic (token bucket algorithm)
  - Returns Retry-After header value when limited

Challenge 3: [Retry Pattern]
  Build a "smart retry" system that:
  - Learns from past failures (shorter retry if usually fast)
  - Adjusts retry delay based on response time percentiles
  - Stops retrying if error rate > 50% in last 60 seconds
  - Reports: retry rate, success rate, avg attempts to succeed

Challenge 4: [Circuit Breaker + Retry]
  Create a "resilient service mesh" with:
  - 5 services, each with their own circuit breaker
  - Retry with backoff per service
  - Service discovery (failover to backup if primary is open)
  - Real-time health dashboard (async terminal output)

Challenge 5: [Async Pipeline]
  Implement an async "stream processing engine":
  - Sources: multiple async generators (Kafka, WebSocket, file)
  - Operators: filter, map, flatmap, window, aggregate
  - Sinks: database, file, HTTP endpoint
  - Backpressure: sink can slow down source
  - Process 10,000 events/second target throughput

Challenge 6: [Work Stealing + Dynamic Scaling]
  Build an "auto-scaling worker pool":
  - Starts with 5 workers
  - Monitors queue depth every second
  - Scales UP if queue > 100 items (add 2 workers, max 20)
  - Scales DOWN if queue < 10 items (remove 1 worker, min 2)
  - Workers gracefully finish current task before removal

Challenge 7: [Complete System]
  Build a "mini async microservice framework" that includes:
  - Service registration and discovery
  - Async RPC between services (using asyncio.Queue)
  - Circuit breaker on all inter-service calls
  - Rate limiting per service
  - Health checks with auto-restart of failed services
  - Metrics collection (calls, latency, errors per service)
  Test with: UserService calling OrderService calling PaymentService
```

sections.title: Best Practices Cheatsheet — Final 7 Coding Challenges — Debugging & Best Practices
sections.body:
```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  CODING CHALLENGES — Debugging & Best Practices              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Challenge 1:
  "Find all the bugs" — given this broken async code:
  def fetch_all(urls):
      results = []
      for url in urls:
          result = fetch(url)  # Bug 1
          results.append(result)
      return results
  
  async def process():
      data = fetch_all(urls)     # Bug 2
      time.sleep(2)              # Bug 3
      task = create_task(save()) # Bug 4
  
  Fix all bugs, explain each one, and write tests to verify
  the fixed version is correct.

Challenge 2:
  Build an "async code linter" (static analyzer) that scans
  Python files and reports:
  - time.sleep() in async functions
  - Missing await on known async functions
  - asyncio.run() inside async functions
  - Bare except clauses that might catch CancelledError
  Use ast module to parse and analyze Python source files.

Challenge 3:
  Create a "performance profiler" for async code that:
  - Measures time spent in each coroutine
  - Identifies the top 5 slowest coroutines
  - Reports event loop blocking incidents (> 50ms)
  - Shows concurrency utilization (avg tasks running)
  - Generates a performance report

Challenge 4:
  Write a "chaos monkey" for async testing that:
  - Randomly injects CancelledError (5% of awaits)
  - Randomly slows down operations (add 0-500ms delay)
  - Randomly raises network errors (10% of HTTP calls)
  - Verifies your async code handles all failures correctly
  - Reports which failure modes were NOT handled

Challenge 5:
  Debug this real-world bug: "Our async web scraper works
  perfectly for 10 minutes then completely stops making requests."
  Write a diagnostic tool that:
  - Monitors queue depths over time
  - Detects deadlocks (all tasks waiting on each other)
  - Identifies task leaks (tasks that never complete)
  - Shows event loop health metrics every 10 seconds

Challenge 6:
  Build a "migration validator" that:
  - Takes sync code and async code that should be equivalent
  - Runs both with the same inputs
  - Verifies they produce identical outputs
  - Reports performance difference (speedup ratio)
  - Catches async bugs: race conditions, missing awaits

Challenge 7: [CAPSTONE CHALLENGE]
  Build a complete "Async URL Shortener Service" that demonstrates
  ALL concepts from this course:
  - FastAPI async endpoints (create, redirect, stats)
  - asyncpg for async PostgreSQL (store URLs)
  - aioredis for async caching (cache popular URLs)
  - Rate limiting (10 req/sec per IP)
  - Circuit breaker on DB calls
  - Background task: async analytics aggregation
  - Graceful shutdown handling
  - Full error handling with structured logging
  - asyncio.Semaphore for concurrent DB connections
  - Producer-consumer for analytics events
  - Health check endpoint showing all component status
```
